values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/blindsucker2 ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Blind Sucker #2: nightly fee $20; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Boating access site on the Blind Sucker Flooding; paddlers' carry-in access about 10 yards from the parking area or directly from some campsites.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/blindsucker2 ('There are vault toilets', 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well', 'A boating access site is located on the Blind Sucker Flooding', 'Carry-in access is located approximately 10 yards from the parking area or directly from some campsites'), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/blindsucker2 ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis', 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay') + amenity table ('Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com': no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 31 sites, 'ideal for tent and small trailer camping' (the DNR's standard state forest wording). No length limit posted. One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/blindsucker2 ('Offering 31 sites, it's ideal for tent and small trailer camping', 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + amenity table (31 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Many sites right on the lake.  --AWH
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 31 tent/small-trailer sites, $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport (fees now on the entry, were inherited), no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, boat access on the Blind Sucker Flooding, first-come only (confirmed), 15-day max (now on the entry); season open all year, roads not plowed (already manual, matches). --AWH 'many sites right on the lake' kept; 'First come first served' dropped as redundant with booking.fcfs.
